history.rationale: Position V437 (full-length V507) directly engages the m102.4 heavy chain CDRs; the bulkier isoleucine sterically hinders antibody binding while remaining fully compatible with ephrin-B2/B3 engagement.
V437I (corresponding to V507I in standard full-length numbering) is the primary canonical m102.4 escape substitution, generating steric clash with the antibody while preserving ephrin binding.

Position D398 (full-length D468) forms critical electrostatic contacts with m102.4; mutating to asparagine removes the salt bridge to disrupt antibody binding while preserving the receptor interaction interface.
D398N (standard D468N) disrupts the electrostatic network and hydrogen bonding with m102.4 heavy chain CDRs while maintaining receptor interaction.
Alanine substitution at D398 removes the negative charge and side-chain contacts necessary for m102.4 recognition without destabilizing the core beta-propeller fold.
D398A removes key m102.4 contact contacts, providing robust neutralization escape with minor reduction in ephrin-B2 affinity.
Truncating the hydrophobic side chain at V437 disrupts van der Waals packing against m102.4 CDR loops while largely maintaining functional receptor binding.
V437A perturbs the hydrophobic interface with m102.4, though it provides slightly lower escape potency than the bulkier V437I substitution.
Eliminating the tyrosine hydroxyl at Y438 abrogates key hydrogen-bonding interactions with m102.4 paratope residues while preserving aromatic packing in the receptor-binding domain.
Y438F selectively eliminates the phenolic hydroxyl interaction with m102.4 while preserving hydrophobic packing essential for receptor complex stability.
Position Q420 contacts the peripheral epitope of m102.4; mutating to alanine reduces polar complementarity with the antibody while sparing essential receptor contacts.
Q420A alters peripheral epitope contacts, conferring moderate escape while maintaining overall head domain fold.
Introducing a positively charged lysine at Q420 creates local electrostatic and steric clashes with m102.4 without interfering with ephrin-B2/B3 binding geometry.
Q420K introduces a positive charge clashing with m102.4 paratope residues but poses a slightly higher risk to local surface stability.
Introducing a negative charge at N439 alters the electrostatic surface potential of the antibody footprint, favoring immune escape while maintaining regional backbone conformation.
N439D introduces a charge inversion in the loop contacting m102.4, promoting escape with moderate tolerance for ephrin binding.
Alanine replacement at D440 alters the local electrostatic network recognized by m102.4 with minimal disruption to the adjacent ephrin-binding pocket.
D440A removes acidic interaction points along the antibody-binding ridge, providing moderate antibody escape.
Neutralizing E435 weakens electrostatic contacts with the m102.4 paratope while retaining acceptable stability of the surrounding beta-sheet scaffold.
E435A disrupts m102.4 salt-bridge contacts but has a lower escape contribution compared to the 437 and 398 hotspots.
